title: Frontend: Match Pair Game
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Match Pair Game. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Four cards[data-card=0..3] have pairs A,B,A,B. Hidden text ?, reveal on click. Ignore already revealed/matched cards. Match locks both, incrementing [data-testid=matched] by two. A mismatch locks further flips until Resolve[data-action=resolve] hides the pair. This button injects timeout completion deterministically. Restart resets all.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent cards by stable pair IDs and card-instance IDs.
alternativeApproaches: Add a reduced-motion mode and an accessible announcement strategy that preserves the puzzle’s rules.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Same card twice; match; mismatch delay.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
